# Acanthosis nigricans

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Pediatrics > Pediatric dermatology > Acanthosis nigricans*

[Original Article Link](/library/U80bN3)

---

## Summary

<u>Acanthosis</u> nigricans is a dermatological condition of <u>hyperkeratosis</u> characterized by velvety, <u>hyperpigmented</u> <u>plaques</u> that are most frequently located in <u>intertriginous areas</u> such as the <u>axillae</u> or groin. It is often caused by an underlying metabolic or endocrine condition, e.g., <u>diabetes</u> or <u>obesity</u>. <u>Acanthosis</u> nigricans may also be genetic or associated with the use of certain medications (e.g., <u>corticosteroids</u>, <u>oral contraceptives</u>). <u>Benign acanthosis nigricans</u> must be distinguished from <u>malignant acanthosis nigricans</u>, which is the cutaneous manifestation of an underlying <u>malignancy</u>. <u>Acanthosis</u> nigricans is a <u>clinical diagnosis</u>, but testing is indicated to identify the underlying cause. Treatment is focused on the underlying cause and may include cosmetic treatment if requested by the patient.

---

## Etiology

* Benign acanthosis nigricans

* Metabolic and endocrine conditions, e.g.: [[1]](/library/sIWtV50)[[2]](/library/HIWKV50)

* <u>Diabetes</u>

* <u>Obesity</u> (sometimes referred to as pseudoacanthosis nigricans) [[3]](/library/Wk1P5S0)

* <u>Cushing syndrome</u>

* <u>Polycystic ovarian syndrome</u>

* Drug-induced <u>acanthosis</u> nigricans (e.g., <u>glucocorticoids</u>, <u>oral contraceptives</u>, <u>testosterone</u>, <u>protease inhibitors</u>) [[4]](/library/lPWvUl0)

* Genetic factors

* Familial <u>acanthosis</u> nigricans: <u>autosomal dominant inheritance</u> [[3]](/library/Wk1P5S0)

* A manifestation of certain genetic syndromes [[4]](/library/lPWvUl0)

* See also “<u>Malignant acanthosis nigricans</u>.” [[1]](/library/sIWtV50)

---

## Pathophysiology

The stimulation of <u>insulin</u>, <u>IGF</u>, and/or other growth factor (e.g., <u>fibroblast</u> growth factor) <u>receptors</u> leads to <u>epidermal</u> <u>hyperplasia</u>, <u>fibroblast</u> <u>proliferation</u>, and <u>hyperkeratosis</u>. [[1]](/library/sIWtV50)[[2]](/library/HIWKV50)

---

## Clinical features

* Appearance [[1]](/library/sIWtV50)[[2]](/library/HIWKV50)

* <u>Hyperpigmented</u>, velvety, and scaly patches or <u>plaques</u>

* Thickening of <u>skin</u> that can develop into papillomatous lesions

* Location [[1]](/library/sIWtV50)[[2]](/library/HIWKV50)

* Typically affects <u>intertriginous areas</u> (e.g., <u>axillae</u>, groin) and/or the back of the neck

* Distribution is usually symmetrical.

## Management

* Identify and treat the underlying <u>cause of acanthosis nigricans</u> (e.g., discontinue offending medications, <u>screen for diabetes</u>, <u>cancer screening</u> if there is concern for <u>malignant acanthosis nigricans</u>).  [[1]](/library/sIWtV50)[[5]](/library/oad0lo0)[[6]](/library/6adjlo0)

* Refer patients who request cosmetic treatment of <u>skin</u> lesions to dermatology; treatment options include: [[5]](/library/oad0lo0)[[6]](/library/6adjlo0)

* Topical agents (e.g., <u>retinoids</u>, <u>keratolytics</u>, <u>calcipotriene</u>)

* Chemical peels

* Oral <u>retinoids</u> (e.g., <u>isotretinoin</u>)

* Laser therapy





> [!WARNING]
> Consider underlying <u>malignancy</u> in patients with a severe or atypical presentation (e.g., lesions with rapid onset of lesions, widespread distribution, and/or <u>mucosal</u> surface involvement). [[1]](/library/sIWtV50)




> [!TIP]
> <u>Acanthosis</u> nigricans is a <u>clinical diagnosis</u>. Treatment of the underlying cause can resolve or improve the appearance of the <u>skin</u> lesions. [[5]](/library/oad0lo0)[[6]](/library/6adjlo0)
